To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Rho family GTPases activate ERKs by stimulating PAKs which phosphorylate MEK1 on a critical serine residue.

Rho family proteins cooperate with Raf  1 to activate the mitogen activated protein (MAP) kinase cascade and the transcriptional response to mitogens, and that this is accomplished by phosphorylation of MEK1 by a MAP kinase activated kinase, PAK.
Rho family proteins cooperate with Raf 11 to stimulate MEK1 and ERKs and that PAKs mediate this effect through phosphorylation of MEK1 at Ser298.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the MAP kinase pathway, which is a major signaling mechanism that transduces growth factor signals to regulate gene expression and cellular proliferation.
the mechanisms by which extracellular signals regulate the activity of MAP kinase signaling pathways and their downstream transcription factors.
the mechanisms of signal transduction and gene regulation in normal and transformed cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ERK pathway is regulated by Rho family GTPases through a PAK1 dependent phosphorylation of MEK1 on serine 298.
PAK1, a Rho family GTPase effector protein, phosphorylates MEK, a MAP kinase kinase, on Ser298.
Rho GTP binding proteins activate the ERK cascade via PAK1 and that PAK1 is a key regulator of the ERK cascade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Rho family small guanosine triphosphatases (GTPases) Rac1 and CDC42HS cooperate with the serine/threonine kinase Raf 1 to stimulate the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAP kinase) cascade.
the Rho family of GTPases, which activate the SAPK pathway, can also stimulate the ERK pathway through a mechanism that involves phosphorylation of MEK1 by PAK1.
PAK1 phosphorylation of MEK1 on S298 is required for MEK1 binding to Raf1 and for MEK1 activation by Rho family small guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase) proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Rho family proteins can cooperate with Raf to activate the ERKS pathway.
Rho family proteins, which regulate JNK, cooperate with Raf1 to activate MEK1 and ERKs.
the MAPK pathways can be cross-communicated.
